COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
CLCON No.275 of 2023
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Alok Mahra, Advocate for the 
petitioners.
The petitioners have brought to the 
notice of the Court that judgment and order 
dated 08.08.2019, passed by the Division 
Bench of this Court in WPSB No.68 of 
2013, Jagdish Chandra Kandpal and 
Others Vs. State of Uttarakhand and 
others, has been wilfully disobeyed by the 
respondent-contemnor. 
The Court posed a question to learned 
counsel for the petitioners as to how a 
contempt petition may now be entertained 
after lapse of almost three years from the 
date, on which the contempt was alleged to 
have been committed, in view of Section 20 
of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 (“the 
Act”)? He would submit that after the order 
dated 08.08.2019, a representation was 
given by the petitioner. Long thereafter, a 
tentative seniority list has been prepared, 
which is not in accordance with the order. 
The question is whether a party may 
extend the period of limitation under 
Section 20 of the Act, by way of filing some 
representation in between? 
The Court will hear on this issue on 
09.10.2023.
 (Ravindra Maithani J.) 
26.09.2023
RV

S. Bisht, learned S.C. for the State.
3. The order passed by the writ Court is dated
08.08.2019 whereby State Government was directed to take 
necessary steps to revise the seniority list of Deputy 
Collectors in terms of order passed by the Division Bench. 
However, the order dated 08.08.2019 was not complied with 
by the respondent-State on the ground that the Special 
Leave Petition was pending before the Apex Court. Now it is 
admitted to both the parties that the SLP filed by the State,
which was converted into civil appeal, has now been 
dismissed vide judgment dated 29.07.2026. The order 
passed by the writ Court is still not being complied with.
4. Learned CSC appearing for the State made a 
statement, on the basis of instructions, that the matter is 
being examined at the level of government.
5. List this matter on 28.09.2026.
6. It is expected that by that time, the order passed by 
writ Court shall be complied with.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 24.08.2026 R.Dang

court has not been complied with.
5. Learned State Counsel made a 
request to place the matter on 
30.09.2026 to apprise the Court as to 
what has happened to the order passed 
by writ court.
6. On his request, put up on

UKHC010155842023
CLCON/275/2023
Jagdish Chandra Kandpal and Others
--Petitioners
 Versus
Shailesh Bagoli
--Respondent
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, learned Senior 
Advocate assisted by Mr. Rajesh Pandey, 
learned counsel for the petitioners.
2. Mr. Puran Singh Bisht, learned CSC
with Mr. Ganesh Kandpal, learned Deputy 
AG and Mr. Jagdish Singh Bisht, learned 
Standing Counsel for the State of 
Uttarakhand.
3. The present contempt petition has 
been filed by the petitioner for willful, 
disobedience of the judgment and order 
dated 08.08.2019 passed by the Division 
Bench of this Court.
4. It is contended by learned Senior 
Advocate for the petitioner that order dated 
08.08.2019 passed by the Division Bench of 
this Court has not been complied with, 
whereby the respondents were directed to 
revise the seniority list of Deputy Collectors 
in terms of the observations made in the 
said order and to extend the benefit of their 
regular appointment w.e.f. 08.04.2010 
treated as relating back to the period from 
01.10.2007.
5. Against the said order, four special 
leave petitions were filed before the Apex 
Court including by the respondents in the 
writ petition, who were direct recruits. All  those SLPs were dismissed and the State 
Government was directed to issue a revised 
seniority list of Deputy Collectors within a 
period of three months from the date of 
judgment i.e. 29.07.2026.
6. Today, learned CSC has supplied 
instructions to the Court date 29.09.2026, 
which are taken on record. On the basis of 
those instructions, it was contended that the 
State is sincerely making efforts to comply
with the order passed by the writ Court. It is 
also submitted that three months’ time will
come to an end on 29.10.2026.
7. Since the respondents have lost before 
the Apex Court, in such view of the matter, 
it is expected by the respondents￾contemnors to comply with the order dated 
08.08.2019 passed by the Division Bench in 
its letter and spirit in between.
8. List this matter on 30.10.2026.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 30.09.2026
R.Bisht
